key_insight: An equivariant graph neural network can predict frequency-dependent dynamic polarizability tensors of organic molecules with TD-DFT-like fidelity, enabling fast optical-property estimation.
engineering_relevance: This provides a scalable surrogate for quantum-chemical calculations, accelerating screening and simulation of photoactive molecules for organic photovoltaic device design.
method: Uses 3D molecular geometry and UV-vis spectra as inputs.
Predicts complex-valued, frequency-dependent dynamic polarizability tensors directly.
Evaluates performance on QM9 and Harvard organic photovoltaic datasets and validates in device-level optical simulations.
evidence_signal: The model reproduced key polarizability features across both datasets and achieved agreement with TD-DFT-based device simulations, including charge carrier generation rates with R² = 0.94.
watch_item: Accuracy and transferability may still depend on the quality and coverage of training data, especially for molecules or spectral regimes outside the training distribution.
paper_title: Accelerating dynamic polarizability calculations of organic molecules using equivariant graph neural networks
